purpose: Prove that separate AI sessions can repair bounded RCL-owned server transaction, authority and reactive-state semantics without inheriting the browser-only K02 eligible-cell authority.
rules: Each generator sees only mutated candidates, server intent and deterministic loopback failure diagnostics.
Canonical files, mutation implementation and oracle edits are absent from the generator workspace.
Each session is fresh, ephemeral and read-only and cannot edit the authoritative repository, tests, thresholds or evidence.
The evaluator applies only the exact file/old/new edit returned under the frozen JSON Schema.
Every repair must restore exact canonical bytes and pass real loopback state, observe, governed rule and negative-route replay.
Three unique sessions, the separately frozen 20-round server runtime receipt and GitHub-hosted replay are required.

trials.intent: Repair addTodo so one accepted loopback transaction increments the server state exactly once.
Repair addTodo so its required capability matches the declared app.write warrant without weakening authority.
Repair resetTodos so the loopback server returns count zero and canonical last_action reset.

evidenceBoundary: This proves three bounded independent repairs plus local loopback execution for the frozen generated server. It does not prove public-network deployment, production scale, distributed service semantics, arbitrary server generation or K400 completion.
